# THE COLONY CHARTER [italic]The civil charter under which this colony is governed, reprinted here for every resident.[/italic]
## Preamble A colony is a bargain between the people who work it and the power that licenses it. This charter sets out who keeps the records, who signs the ordinances and what every resident is owed, whatever flag flies over the landing pad.
## Article I: The Colony - The colony, its settlements, works and the roads between them form one civil jurisdiction under one Administration. - Colonial law binds every resident, contractor and visitor. Garrison personnel answer to their own codes on base and to colonial law off it.
## Article II: The Administrator - The Colony Administrator heads the civil government, keeps the colony's records and signs its ordinances. - The Deputy Administrator acts in the Administrator's place when the office is vacant, or its holder absent or unable to serve. - No ordinance takes effect until it is posted on this board.
## Article III: Residents - Every resident may petition the office, and every petition receives an answer in writing. - No resident may be held by colonial police for more than seventy-two hours without charge. - Air, water and emergency shelter are owed to every person in the colony, whether their contract is paid up or not.
## Article IV: Security - The garrison defends the colony and answers mass emergencies. It does not govern. - Curfews, security zones and operations inside the settlements are set in consultation with the Administrator.
## Article V: Safety [italic]Written into colonial charters across the frontier after Albacetire, 2168, where a drill site broke into trapped gas and more than twelve thousand people died because nobody was ready.[/italic] - No excavation proceeds without a gas and ground survey filed with this office. - The atmosphere monitoring network may not be switched off, sold or leased. - Every block has a posted shelter, and the list is kept current.
